depeche-mode>david-bowie.found: I listened to David Bowie a lot when I was a teenager. The place that he seemed to be singing from is the place that I wanted to go to.
depeche-mode>david-bowie.citation: Dave Gahan to CNN (2012): "I listened to David Bowie a lot when I was a teenager. The place that he seemed to be singing from is the place that I wanted to go to."

depeche-mode>the-clash.found: The same thing happened when punk rock came along and I heard the Clash for the first time. I was 16 or 17 years old. It made me feel like I belonged to something.
depeche-mode>the-clash.citation: Dave Gahan to CNN (2012), on punk: "I heard the Clash for the first time. I was 16 or 17 years old. It made me feel like I belonged to something."

depeche-mode>velvet-underground.found: On the record I do a cover of a Velvet Underground song, and I think for me they were one of the most important bands. I like their darkness but I also like the pop-side of the Velvet Underground.
depeche-mode>velvet-underground.citation: Martin Gore to Release Magazine (2003): "I think for me they were one of the most important bands. I like their darkness but I also like the pop-side of the Velvet Underground."

depeche-mode>suicide.found: You may not have heard of American duo Suicide, but you will have heard of the groups they influenced. Depeche Mode, New Order, Moby, Radiohead - almost every techno or industrial act, or rock band that uses synthesisers, has cited Suicide as an influence.
depeche-mode>suicide.citation: The Jewish Chronicle: "Depeche Mode, New Order, Moby, Radiohead - almost every techno or industrial act, or rock band that uses synthesisers, has cited Suicide as an influence."
depeche-mode>suicide.note: The Guardian sentence in the old citation was not found on any page; Wikipedia's Depeche Mode article footnotes Gore to The Times via Nobahkt's book Suicide: No Compromise (2004) p.166 (not readable online).

new-order>suicide.found: Acts such as New Order, Air, Daft Punk and Aphex Twin have all cited the group as a musical influence.

the-smiths>bert-jansch.found: For example, in my case, I didn't really do a lot of interviews in the early Smiths days but when I was asked about guitar playing, when I had to really nail it down it was Nile Rodgers , Bert Jansch and James Williamson from The Stooges.

talking-heads>david-bowie.found: David Byrne recalled how the Byrds helped him begin the journey to finding his own voice in music after he began life listening to folk artists, and how David Bowie and the Velvet Underground provided his next steps.
talking-heads>david-bowie.citation: Ultimate Classic Rock, reporting David Byrne's Pitchfork interview (2023): the Byrds helped Byrne move on from folk, and David Bowie and the Velvet Underground "provided his next steps".
talking-heads>david-bowie.note: Pitchfork's own page was not located (search returned only write-ups). Far Out (faroutmagazine.co.uk/david-byrne-david-bowie-inspiration/) also quotes Byrne's Pitchfork words on Bowie: "Bowie was on the radio a little bit, and he was a huge influence for a lot of people."

black-flag>bad-brains.found: “I grew up with Bad Brains and they were the first band I saw up close,” he stated. “I mean right in their faces. I saw them open for The Damned in ’79 and a week later at a party it changed my life.
black-flag>bad-brains.citation: Henry Rollins, in a 1990 interview with Elsewhere Magazine (reported by Far Out): "I grew up with Bad Brains and they were the first band I saw up close... I saw them open for The Damned in '79 and a week later at a party it changed my life."
black-flag>bad-brains.note: Speaker is Rollins, who joined Black Flag in 1981 (after Bad Brains had changed his life); Black Flag itself formed in 1976, a year before Bad Brains, so the owner may prefer to treat this as Rollins's influence rather than the band's.

pavement>sonic-youth.found: BN : It’s the only significant tour we’ve done opening. I was outvoted 4–1. I didn’t want to do it. On the tour, there were good things and bad things about it. You’ve got to understand that Pavement could’ve played venues close to that big on their own back then. But we all got along well, and were huge fans. EVOL and Sister changed my life, and “The World Looks Red” is my favorite Sonic Youth song.
pavement>sonic-youth.citation: Bob Nastanovich to The A.V. Club (2022), on touring with Sonic Youth: "we all got along well, and were huge fans. EVOL and Sister changed my life, and 'The World Looks Red' is my favorite Sonic Youth song." Mark Ibold added: "we were sort of influenced by Sonic Youth in that respect."

pavement>echo-and-the-bunnymen.found: I mean, all the bands we really loved turned us onto great bands. R.E.M. turned me on to Mission of Burma, Wire, and Big Star. Even the Velvet Underground and Echo and the Bunnymen turned us onto Leonard Cohen and Television.

R.E.M. turned me on to Mission of Burma, Wire, and Big Star. Even the Velvet Underground and Echo and the Bunnymen turned us onto Leonard Cohen and Television."
pavement>echo-and-the-bunnymen.note: The AV Club's own framing: a generous ethos "learned from their own heroes, including R.E.M., Sonic Youth, and Echo & the Bunnymen". The Killing Moon cover is in Wikipedia (Major Leagues EP), not on this page.

Pavement's Scott Kannberg'.
